correctness.rationale: Reconstructed without relying solely on the inaccessible original paper: for each complex multi-index alpha with |alpha|=m, Fourier integration on coordinatewise circles inside the ell_p unit ball gives |a_alpha| ≤ (m^m/alpha^alpha)^(1/p)||P||_p, with p=infinity interpreted via unit polydisc. Weighted AM-GM/Hölder maximizes |u^alpha| over ||u||_t≤1 at (alpha^alpha/m^m)^(1/t), including t=infinity. Thus each coefficient term is ≤(m^m/alpha^alpha)^(1/p-1/t)||P||_p||u||_t^m. If t≤p the exponent is nonpositive and the pure monomial z1^m gives sharp C=1. If p<t, only alpha with support at most k=min(s,m) matter; splitting a part ≥2 strictly reduces alpha^alpha until exactly k parts, while strict convexity of x log x shows minimizers have balanced parts q,q+1 for m=kq+r. A monomial with precisely those exponents and diagonal u_j=(alpha_j/m)^(1/t), or 1 at infinity, attains both optimizations, including all m,s,n,1<=p,t<=infinity. Strict support growth through k=m follows from a strict split. No enumeration purports to prove arbitrary m.
